notes:
Identity assessment: the supplied canonical text is a complete author working paper, University of Innsbruck Working Papers in Economics and Statistics 2011-08, dated March 8, 2011, by Michael Kirchler, Jürgen Huber and Thomas Stöckl, with the matching title Thar She Bursts – Reducing Confusion Reduces Bubbles. The cache header names DOI 10.1257/aer.102.2.865, and the end matter calls this a modified version forthcoming in American Economic Review. It is primary author research, not a secondary summary, but is not the cited 2012 journal pagination/version; supplied journal locator p. 875 cannot be directly resolved in this working paper. No PDF path was supplied; no PDF acquisition or rendering performed.

Target ambiguity: the neutral description identifies both RAD mispricing and RD overvaluation and declining FV/increasing C/A (T1), but does not specify the comparison, outcome, pooled versus pairwise test, or context contrast. No selection was made using numeric agreement or row order. Candidate main tests, working-paper Table 6 p. 11 (each pair lists printed RAD then RD difference in means, Z, and significance bound where printed): RQ1 pooled T1+T2 vs T3+T4, N=24 markets: 0.080, Z=−0.751, no p bound; 0.152*, Z=−2.078, p<0.05. T1 vs T3, N=12 markets: 0.109, Z=−0.801; 0.337, Z=−1.601 (neither has a printed numeric p/bound). T2 vs T4, N=12 markets: 0.052, Z=−0.641; −0.033, Z=−1.121 (neither has a printed numeric p/bound). RQ2 pooled T1+T3 vs T2+T4, N=24 markets: 0.307**, Z=−3.753, p<0.01; 0.171*, Z=−1.963, p<0.05. T1 vs T2, N=12 markets: 0.335*, Z=−2.402, p<0.05; 0.357**, Z=−2.882, p<0.01. T3 vs T4, N=12 markets: 0.278**, Z=−2.882, p<0.01; −0.014, Z=−0.160, no printed numeric p/bound. Asterisks signify printed significance levels, not exact p. These are candidate evidence, not accepted field values. Section 3.3.2 pp. 12–13 also compares T5 gold-mine context with T1: printed T5 outcome levels RAD 0.16 and RD -0.07, exact same-outcome Mann-Whitney p=0.025 and p=0.004, respectively; these outcome levels are not printed mean differences. Table A2 p. 21 prints T5 means 0.157, −0.069 and T1 means 0.414, 0.296; Table 4 p. 9 instead prints T1 RD 0.297. No differences were computed or precision reconciled. Section 3.3.3 p. 15 additionally compares T6 rounds against T1 and T5; these are robustness candidates, not selected targets. Appendix B Table A3 p. 22 reports separate exclusions-based robustness tests, N=20 pooled and N=10 pairwise, dropping the highest-RAD market per treatment; no robustness value was substituted for a main test.

Analytic-unit assessment: Mann-Whitney tests compare markets, not 360 recruited student contributors or 10 periods per market. Main Table 6 explicitly prints N=24 for pooled tests and N=12 for pairwise tests; no N was inferred from degrees of freedom. The six markets per treatment in section 2.5 support candidate T1-versus-T5 analytic N 6 + 6 = 12 mutually exclusive markets (60 + 60 = 120 student contributors at ten traders per market, not analytic N). This candidate sum is not accepted because the comparison remains ambiguous. No main-test exclusions are stated; the explicit one-market-per-treatment exclusions belong only to Table A3 robustness checks. No single common model N spans all plausible targets.

Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders only.
